critique.paragraph: This map teaches parameter-space-as-landscape (Edge G) or emergence-at-threshold (Edge E), not apparatus-as-phenomenon (Edge H). The λ gradient is visually clear—order to edge to chaos—and the corridor makes it walkable, but the phenomenon appears pre-existing rather than enacted by observation. The walker is a probe traversing an independent spectrum, not an apparatus co-constituting what it measures. Edge H requires the measurement act to *make* the phenomenon; here, the phenomenon (the gradient) exists whether the walker is present or not. The visual grammar is strong but addresses the wrong claim.
strengths: Clear visual gradient from crystalline blue (order) through green edge zone to orange dissolution (chaos)
Corridor geometry makes the spectrum legibly walkable—depth IS λ
The green zone at λ≈0.4 is visually distinct as the edge of chaos
Multiple reinforcing visual systems: particle density, color temperature, formation coherence
weaknesses: The λ spectrum appears pre-existing and independent of the walker—no evidence the apparatus *makes* the phenomenon
Walker functions as probe/measurer, not as co-constituent of what's observed
Missing the core H claim: different observational paths should yield different readings of the same object
The gradient is position-dependent but not observation-dependent—standing at λ=0.4 always yields the same result
No central ambiguous object that the apparatus's approach determines (wave vs particle, order vs chaos)
next_gen_hints: Add a central phenomenon that reads as 'ordered crystal' when approached from the λ=0 end, 'chaotic particle cloud' when approached from the λ=1 end—same object, different apparatus-cuts
Split the corridor into two parallel paths (one ordered-frame, one chaotic-frame) that yield contradictory measurements of the same centerline phenomenon
Make the gradient visibly responsive to player attention: the phenomenon at position X changes when you look at it vs when you turn away
Place measurement apparatus artifacts (frames, lenses, grids) along the path that are visibly part of what they're measuring—the frame and the framed as one system
Show the 'cut' that produces observer and observed: a bifurcation point where the path's choice determines which phenomenon appears ahead
critique.edge_reads_as: G (parameter space as landscape) or E (emergence at threshold)
